section_summary: This section chiefly documents narcotics cases in and around Japan during 1935, including opium brought from Honolulu and Karafuto, morphine smuggling from Germany, arrests at Kobe and Tokyo, and official exchanges between the State and Treasury Departments. It also covers Japanese efforts to rehabilitate narcotic addicts, an American company's proposed addiction treatment called “Rossium,” and allegations linking traffickers to a former Osaka procurator. The section ends with the opening portion of a confidential report assessing anti-smuggling controls at the port of Kobe.

subfiles.title: Arrest of an Opium Smuggler: A Mysterious Person on the Chichibu Maru
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest at Yokohama of a Korean passenger carrying opium allegedly obtained in Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: Water Police arrested Kin Ohitsu on the Chichibu Maru from Honolulu with opium hidden in a watch and bedding, allegedly for sale in Japan and Korea.

subfiles.title: Telegram Requesting Details of the Chichibu Maru Seizure
subfiles.about: Orders the Embassy to obtain information on the Yokohama opium seizure so that authorities can investigate in Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: Department asks the Embassy for full details of the March 21 Chichibu Maru seizure for a Honolulu investigation, unless Japanese authorities already supplied them.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch on Morphine Smuggling by the Cheribon Maru Crew
subfiles.about: Transmits a Tokyo Embassy despatch concerning morphine smuggling to the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: State encloses Despatch No. 1203 on morphine smuggled by Cheribon Maru crewmen and advises exchanging narcotics-police information via the Embassy, not the Kobe consul.

subfiles.title: Instruction on Embassy Control of Narcotics Information Exchanges
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to centralize official exchanges with Japanese authorities about narcotics smuggling.
subfiles.summary: The Department acknowledged the Embassy's report on morphine smuggling aboard the Cheribon Maru and praised the Kobe consul's initiative. It instructed the Embassy to tell the consul and Treasury representatives not to approach local Japanese officials without Embassy authorization, while continuing to forward press and independently obtained information.

subfiles.title: Letter Transmitting Information on the Japanese Addicts' Relief Association
subfiles.about: Sends Fuller a summary of a Japanese Foreign Office report on a private association assisting drug addicts.
subfiles.summary: Kusama sends Fuller a summary of the Tokyo association for the relief of drug addicts, obtained through the Japanese Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Association for Relief of Narcotic Addicts in Japan
subfiles.from: Association for Relief of Narcotic Addicts in Japan
subfiles.to: Shiko Kusama and Stuart J. Fuller
subfiles.about: Summarizes the association's organization, finances, treatment home, and expansion plans.
subfiles.summary: The Tokyo addicts' relief association, organized February 1933, treats indigent mostly Korean addicts, does preventive propaganda, and plans a larger home and an Oshima farm.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Kusama's Report for the Public Health Service
subfiles.about: Forwards Kusama's letter and association report for the United States Public Health Service.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Kusama's April 4 letter and addicts' association summary to the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Kusama's Report for the Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Forwards duplicate copies of the association material for the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Department sends two copies of Kusama's April 4 letter and association report to the Commissioner of Narcotics.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Shiko Kusama
subfiles.about: Thanks Kusama for the report on the Association for Relief of Narcotic Addicts in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Fuller thanks Kusama for the association summary, read with great interest.

subfiles.title: Treasury Acknowledgment of Public Health Service Material
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the association report intended for the Public Health Service.
subfiles.summary: Treasury acknowledges State's April 19 letter and the report on the Japanese narcotic addicts' relief association.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japanese Narcotic Factories at Mukden
subfiles.about: Refers researchers to a letter transmitting a Shanghai agent's report on Japanese narcotic factories at Mukden.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Treasury letter on Japanese narcotic factories in Mukden, from a March 30 Shanghai agent's report.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japanese Loans for Poppy Cultivation in Jehol
subfiles.about: Points to a report about Japanese loans encouraging poppy cultivation in Jehol.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Treasury letter transmitting an April 1 report on Japanese financing of poppy cultivation in Jehol.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Heroin and Opium Operations in Jehol
subfiles.about: Refers to a report on heroin manufacture and opium collection in Jehol under Japanese sponsorship.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: heroin made by the Foochee and Hoh-chee companies with alleged Japanese backing, and Jehol opium collected by the Dai Man Company.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1260: Tsunemitsu, Trafficker in Narcotic Drugs
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the rejection of appeals by three men convicted of smuggling morphine derivatives from Germany into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew reviewed the case of Katsutoshi Tsunemitsu, Kyoji Kitada, and Sennosuke Asai, who had been convicted of importing benzyl and benzoyl morphine. The Japan Chronicle reported that the Supreme Court rejected their appeals and left fines totaling about ¥270,000 in force.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch on the Tsunemitsu Case
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew's despatch on the Tsunemitsu morphine-smuggling case to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: State sends two confidential copies of Despatch No. 1260 on Tsunemitsu's smuggling of benzyl and benzoyl morphine from Germany into Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of “15 Opium Peddlers Held”
subfiles.about: Sends the Commissioner of Narcotics two copies of a Japan Chronicle article about opium peddlers.
subfiles.summary: State encloses the Japan Chronicle's May 1 article on fifteen alleged opium peddlers arrested.

subfiles.title: 15 Opium Peddlers Held
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of a Korean group accused of distributing Sakhalin opium in Japan and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo police found dynamite and sixteen pounds of opium at a Korean dormitory and arrested two men implicating thirteen others, with distribution to Tokyo, Kyoto, Nagasaki and Shanghai using Sakhalin opium.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 476: Arrest of Opium Smugglers at Kobe
subfiles.about: Compares a newspaper account of seven arrests with the official Hyogo Prefecture report.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 476: Inada, Fujita and Nakamura brought about seven pounds of opium from Otomari to Kobe; Inada got six months. Donovan notes the names differ from the newspaper's.

subfiles.title: Kobe Yushin Nippo Account of the Opium-Smuggling Arrests
subfiles.about: Describes a Kobe police raid and a wider Japanese-Chinese opium-smuggling network linked to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Kobe Yushin Nippo: police arrested Inamura, Yuoka, Nakabayashi, Fujioka and others negotiating an opium sale; the network bought opium in Shanghai and used seamen to land it in Karafuto or Hokkaido.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1284: Opium Smuggling from Saghalien to Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of five Japanese accused of smuggling smoking opium from Karafuto.
subfiles.summary: Grew named Gentaro Nakai, Tokuichi Sakamoto, Tsunekichi Fukui, Teru Okamoto, and Kotaro Hashimoto as defendants being held for trial. He enclosed a Japanese Foreign Office note and Metropolitan Police record describing their preliminary examination.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office Note Transmitting the Metropolitan Police Report
subfiles.from: Kuriyama, Chief of the Bureau of Treaties
subfiles.about: Transmits the Japanese Home Affairs Department's report on the Ueno opium arrests.
subfiles.summary: Kuriyama says Neville's March 13 request went to Home Affairs, encloses the Metropolitan Police report, and notes opium law charges in the Tokyo District Court.

subfiles.title: Metropolitan Police Report on the Ueno Opium Case
subfiles.to: Chief of the Sanitary Bureau, Department of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: Details the discovery, participants, movements, and disputed sale of opium brought from Karafuto.
subfiles.summary: Metropolitan Police report: over two hundred momme of opium found at Teru Okamoto's house; Hashimoto allegedly bought 4.3 kan from a Korean in Toyohara, and Nakai was accused of keeping proceeds.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Kobe Despatch No. 476
subfiles.about: Forwards the Kobe consul's report on the arrest of seven alleged opium smugglers.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner two copies of Donovan's May 2 Kobe Despatch No. 476.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo Despatch No. 1284
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew's report on five Japanese charged with smuggling opium from Karafuto.
subfiles.summary: State sends two confidential copies of Despatch No. 1284 on the January 23 arrest of five Japanese bringing smoking opium from Karafuto.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1320: Seizure of Opium from a Korean on the Chichibu Maru
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Provides an initial official Japanese report on the Chichibu Maru opium seizure.
subfiles.summary: In response to the Department's telegram, the Embassy obtained a Kanagawa Prefecture report through the Japanese Foreign Office. Grew emphasized that the main fact useful for investigation was the allegation that a Chinese man named Shen supplied the opium in Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Initial Kanagawa Report on the Chichibu Maru Passenger
subfiles.to: Director, Sanitary Bureau, Department of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes Kim Ung-pil's opium possession and use aboard the Chichibu Maru.
subfiles.summary: Kanagawa report: a Korean Chichibu Maru passenger with a Hawaii opium habit carried liquid, lump and crude opium; referred to the procurator April 18.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Despatch No. 1320
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Embassy despatch transmitting the initial Kanagawa report on the Chichibu Maru case.
subfiles.summary: This is a noisier duplicate of the despatch on the Korean passenger arrested at Yokohama. It again identifies Shen of Honolulu as the potentially useful lead for American investigators.

subfiles.title: Duplicate of the Initial Kanagawa Opium Report
subfiles.to: Director, Sanitary Bureau, Department of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: Duplicates the initial account of the opium found on the Chichibu Maru passenger.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the initial Kanagawa report on the Korean passenger with opium habit and possessions.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1354: Japanese Association for the Relief of Narcotic Addicts
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a newspaper feature about the Tokyo rescue home for narcotic addicts.
subfiles.summary: Grew enclosed a Japan Advertiser clipping describing the association's rescue home in Tokyo. He explained that the director called Takayuki Namae was apparently the same person previously rendered as Takayuki Ikuye, because the relevant character allowed either reading.

subfiles.title: Rescue Home Aids Victims of Drugs
subfiles.about: Describes the treatment, labor, discipline, patients, and finances of a Tokyo rescue home for narcotic addicts.
subfiles.summary: Rescue home shelters about forty-five mostly Korean morphine addicts, treating them without narcotics through discipline, work and mutual encouragement; profiles staff and patients and plans a larger building.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1360: Further Report on the Chichibu Maru Seizure
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a fuller Kanagawa report giving Honolulu addresses and other details in the Kim Ung-pil case.
subfiles.summary: The new report supplied addresses for Shen and other people connected with the case, although the Embassy warned that kana transliteration might be inaccurate. Grew suggested investigating the Century Hospital on Palama Street because Kim said its physician had recommended opium for beriberi.

subfiles.title: Full Kanagawa Report on Kim Ung-pil
subfiles.to: Director, Sanitary Bureau, Department of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: Provides a detailed account of Kim Ung-pil's purchase, concealment, consumption, and possession of opium.
subfiles.summary: Kim Ung-pil said he used opium at Shen's Honolulu home since 1929 and bought opium before sailing on the Chichibu Maru; he was sent to the procurator April 18 but released.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japanese Arms for Iranian Opium
subfiles.about: Points to a letter concerning a proposed exchange of Japanese armaments for Iranian opium.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a British official's information that Japan proposed selling arms to Iran in exchange partly for opium.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 1354 for the Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy despatch and Japan Advertiser clipping about the addicts' relief association.
subfiles.summary: State sends Despatch No. 1354 and its newspaper enclosure to the Commissioner of Narcotics; another copy goes to the Public Health Service.
keywords: Association for Relief of Narcotic Addicts

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 1354 for the Public Health Service
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy despatch and clipping for the United States Public Health Service.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Tokyo report and Japan Advertiser article on the narcotic-addict association to the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Confidential Transmittal of Chichibu Maru Reports to Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends both Embassy reports on Kim Ung-pil and requests information about any Honolulu investigation of Shen.
subfiles.summary: The Department contrasted the Tokyo Asahi allegation of organized smuggling with the official conclusion that the small quantity was for Kim's personal use. It enclosed despatches Nos. 1320 and 1360 and asked Treasury to report any effort to identify Shen in Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Treasury Acknowledgment of Despatch No. 1354
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Tokyo report on the Association for Relief of Narcotic Addicts.
subfiles.summary: Treasury confirms receipt of Despatch No. 1354 and the Japan Advertiser clipping for the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japanese Narcotic Firms in Tianjin
subfiles.about: Refers to Treasury Attaché Nicholson's list of Japanese opium and narcotic firms in Tianjin.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Treasury Attaché Nicholson's June 10 report listing Japanese opium and narcotic firms in the Tianjin Japanese Concession.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Mallinckrodt Trademark Registration in Japan
subfiles.to: State Department file 811.114 N 16-Mallinckrodt Chemical Works/323
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence about registration of the Mallinckrodt script trademark by a Yokohama company.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Treasury letter on Mallinckrodt's concern over trademark registration by Siber, Hegner and Company of Yokohama and possible narcotics implications.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japanese Narcotics Penalties and Acetic Anhydride Exports
subfiles.about: Refers to an instruction transmitting Opium Advisory Committee material on Japanese penalties and chemical exports to China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: inadequate Japanese narcotics penalties and acetic anhydride exports from Japan to China.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1410: “Rossium,” Alleged Specific for Drug Addiction
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Requests information about Rossium before referring its American promoter to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy received a request from the Medico Chemical Corporation to contact Japanese government hospitals about Rossium. Because purported addiction cures could be dangerous, Neville asked the Department for evidence about the preparation's value before taking further action.

subfiles.title: Medico Chemical Corporation Letter Promoting Rossium
subfiles.from: Walter Neumann, Medico Chemical Corporation of America
subfiles.about: Asks for help approaching Japanese government hospitals about the sale of Rossium.
subfiles.summary: Medico Chemical Corporation promotes Rossium as a drug-addiction treatment used in a Chinese hospital, asking the Embassy for Japanese contacts.

subfiles.title: Treasury Letter Enclosing the Honolulu Investigation
subfiles.from: Stephen B. Gibbons, for the Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Transmits the Narcotic Agent's report on Kim Ung-pil and the Honolulu source of his opium.
subfiles.summary: Treasury sends the Honolulu agent's July 20 report on Kim Ung-pil and Shen in the Chichibu Maru matter.

subfiles.title: Honolulu Narcotic Service Report on Kim Ung-pil and Shen
subfiles.to: Harry J. Anslinger, Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Reports the American investigation of Kim Ung-pil's acquisition of opium before sailing for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Honolulu agent Stevenson identifies Kin Oh Hitsu as Kim Ung-pil, an addict; companion statements say a five-tael opium tin bought with his money was partly carried aboard the Chichibu Maru.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Proposed Treasury Jurisdiction over Manchuria
subfiles.from: Stuart J. Fuller, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum opposing the addition of Manchuria to the district of Treasury's representative in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Fuller's reasons why adding Manchuria to the Japan district of Treasury jurisdiction is inadvisable.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Assurance That Manchuria Would Not Be Added
subfiles.from: William Phillips, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Refers to a memorandum recording Treasury's assurance that its Japan district would not be expanded to Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Treasury official Gibbons assured Phillips the proposed Manchuria jurisdiction change would not be made.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 825 Transmitting the Honolulu Investigation
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends the Honolulu findings on Kim Ung-pil for delivery to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 825 encloses the Honolulu investigation of the Chichibu Maru case and directs delivery to Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Honolulu Investigation of Kim Ung-pil
subfiles.about: Summarizes evidence that Kim Ung-pil obtained his opium through other known Honolulu addicts and dealers.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Kim Ung-pil, a notorious addict, bought a five-tael tin through Choi and Ching Dow, smoked some, and carried the rest, prepared opium and a pipe stem to Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to the Medico Chemical Corporation Regarding Rossium
subfiles.about: Advises the company to approach the Japanese consul general in New York about Rossium.
subfiles.summary: Department tells Medico Chemical to take its Rossium proposal to the Japanese consul general in New York.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 826 Concerning Rossium
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Informs the Embassy of the Department's reply to the Rossium promoter.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 826 encloses the Department's letter directing Medico Chemical to the Japanese consul general, referring to Despatch No. 1410.

subfiles.title: Confidential Telegram Ordering Investigations of Japanese Port Controls
subfiles.about: Orders discreet reports on anti-smuggling controls at Yokohama and Kobe for use at the Opium Advisory Committee.
subfiles.summary: Telegram orders Yokohama and Kobe to investigate controls over ships and access to vessels, with reports to Geneva for the November 12 Opium Advisory Committee.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1485: Sennosuke Asai, Narcotics Smuggler
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Reports bribery allegations involving a former Osaka procurator and convicted narcotics smuggler Sennosuke Asai.
subfiles.summary: The Japan Chronicle reported that former procurator Ginzo Mitani had been indicted for accepting approximately ¥16,000 in bribes from Tokuzo Shima, Sennosuke Asai, and others between 1928 and 1932. Neville suggested that further proceedings might disclose details of Japanese narcotics-trafficking operations.

subfiles.title: Confidential Transmittal of the Mitani-Asai Despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards the report on Ginzo Mitani's alleged acceptance of bribes from Sennosuke Asai and others.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Narcotics Commissioner two confidential copies of Despatch No. 1485 on Asai, a Tsunemitsu associate on the confidential list.

subfiles.title: Telegram Concerning Hoshi's Visas and Travel
subfiles.from: American officials in Tokyo, signed Clapham
subfiles.about: Reports visas and stated travel dates for a person named Hoshi.
subfiles.summary: Telegram: Hoshi was granted visas, arriving in San Francisco November 20 and claiming he will return to Japan December 13.

subfiles.title: Control of Smuggling at the Port of Kobe, Japan
subfiles.about: Begins a detailed assessment of controls over arriving, berthed, and departing ships at Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Kobe report: baggage inspection is careful but personal searches limited; Japanese officials vigorously block narcotics entering Japan but make little effort to stop drugs on departing ships.
